segments: The Eighth Dynasty.
The Kings of the Romans.
Nineteen [years].
At the beginning of his reign,
Vologases, king of the Parthians, devastated many regions belonging to the Romans.
Then his sons {recte: Antoninus's sons/associates}, Antoninus and Lucius, went and subjugated the Parthians.
And the Romans had a war against the Germans and the Quadi (Quadi,
or Quadians? {editor's note}) and the Sarmatians and the Dacians.
And Lucius triumphed over them,
and was called Autokrator.
And after nine years he died.
Then Antoninus his brother associated with him in the kingdom Commodus his son.
And when Antoninus fell ill in Pannonia, he died.
And Commodus his son, having reigned thirteen years,
was strangled in the house of Vestilianus.
And lightning fell upon the Capitol,
and burned the libraries and the palace and the House of the Virgins {the Vestals} for six months;
and he was killed.
[Severus,] eighteen years.
In his first year, there was a fierce war against the Jews and the Samaritans.
And from his ninth year until the end of his life, he raised a great persecution against the Christians,
and many bore witness {martyred} and were crowned.
Now when he went against the barbarian people at the foot of the north-western mountain, who greatly troubled the Romans who were on their borders,
he died there.
In other copies:
he was killed.
[Caracalla,] four (seven) years.
He released those who were in exile for the sake of the faith.
Now he was killed in Mesopotamia, between Harran and Edessa.
[Macrinus,] one year.
And in it, the circus of Hephaestus in Rome was burned.
And he was killed in Archelais.
[Antoninus,] who is from Heliogabalus (Elagabalus?), four years.
In his time, Nicopolis of Palestine, which is Emmaus, was built.
Julius Africanus, the writer of the Chronicon, was in charge of its building.
[Alexander,] son of Mamaea, thirteen years.
This Mamaea believed in Christ,
and she greatly helped the Christians.
